translations.text: When we went to the foreign country,

forms.text: ni-misa-namen lu ditanasay nimi-namen ni-mitku tu vagay Darikud

translations.text: we spent the night at Ditanasay, and we slept in Darikud's(unctn) house.
The next morning, we had one bowl of food each.
When we got to the wharf,
the soldiers looked at our names
one after the other, and then we disembarked.
They didn't want the man from Iranmiluk to go first.
The soldiers made him go back in a hurry.
So one of us was left over there.

forms.text: yaru karwan lu dewdew-em dy-aru-pa-sira a-ni-padi/machyura-rana

translations.text: Many, many other foreigners accompanied us.

forms.text: makasasned namen-em nimi-namen ni-makasasned namen di-sinku
ditagen namen u araw-em ni-maligen u araw

translations.text: Looking at the sun, we saw that it was mid-day.
We just had a little money.

forms.text: walem-nem/namen-a k-angay-nemn/namen-a-rana u mavang tu alilu

translations.text: We walked up to where we boarded the bus.
We gave over one hundred dollars and fifty cents over there to get here.
And so we arrived at Taytu and here

translations.text: When I was getting ready to come to this country,

forms.text: ni-myura-sira a-kanu i-ra-ralay ni-mai-sira lu vagay-ku

translations.text: accompanied by the believers, they first went to my house.
There were three of them; Siang had gone

forms.text: ni-mang-an-anau lu karwan nu ili y-arwa

translations.text: to teach in two other villages.
After the house had been all swept (and we had made our trip here),

forms.text: ipanda-ku s-ama-n-kalaku su anem-a-puu a niripi u asa-ka-tau-em

translations.text: I, Saman Kalaku, was the only one that received six hundred dollars.
"I'll take twenty dollars of the money," I said,

forms.text: maniring s-ama-n-kalaku dungyan lu dia kwan-a-m
nun kwan-ku yana-k-angay-rana u niripi-am ka-pitu-araw kwan-ku

translations.text: I'll go now. That was the money for seven days."

forms.text: a-yana-ni-pangep ni-padinga-nina? su ipiveravera su ngusu
a-kanu siken a-kanu vaynget a-kanu alavat

translations.text: some soap, a towel, and a bag.
So he spent one hundred dollars.

forms.text: inyuranayam mang-anak-u-em anu amyan su panchy-an-da-ninyu-em

translations.text: My dear children, when the foreigner in Imurud is lecturing all of you

forms.text: tuka-malu-maluvut anu ipanchi-di-nyu nu tau d-imurud a-dewdew

translations.text: My dear children, when the foreigner in Imurud is lecturing all of you
then take some advice from an old person.
When there's much work to be done,

forms.text: sinu mapasalasala lu chir-chiring nu pangangavangen

translations.text: everybody should obey the commands of the foreigner.
When we're digging every afternoon on the mountain,

forms.text: puken-em marikna-namen-pa kwan-amen a-mangday su araw akak-agep-an/(mangday su agep)

translations.text: Every day and every evening, you come home crying, little children.

forms.text: tau nu kakwa amyan su avang tu titiwen kwan-da

translations.text: A long time ago, there was a ship at Titiwen.

forms.text: ma-chita-da tu madegdeg (imurud nu tau)/(tau d-imurud)

translations.text: Early in the morning, the people from Imurud saw them (ship's crew).

forms.text: sira(unctn) mi-ripu-ripus mang-aep-tamu su matengteng utwen kwan-da

translations.text: His relatives said, "Let's take some cold food

forms.text: ituru-tamu-dira kwan-da m-angay-tamu lu tatala kwan-da

translations.text: to give them, and go over in our boat."

forms.text: nun kwan-da m-angay-sira lu tatala m-angay titiwen.

translations.text: They went by boat to Titiwen,

forms.text: tau nu avang mamimin-sira ni-m-angay lu katyan miwalem lu rerchip

translations.text: All the people from the ship had gone to Katyan and were resting in the cave.
The newcomers with the food pulled the boat up on the shore.
The newcomers with the food pulled the boat up on the shore.

forms.text: ma-chita-da nu dewdew ina-kamu-pa su kanen kwan-da

translations.text: As soon as the foreigners saw it, they said, "Give us some food."

forms.text: ipanchi nu tau i-kongu-kamu-ya chiri-chiring nu dewdew vawden namen kwan-da

translations.text: The newcomers said, "Why are you here?" The foreigners replied, "You've come to bind us?"

forms.text: chiri-chiring nu tau ning kwan-da nukumwanem vawden-tamu sira kwan-da
k-aep-da su talili-da nu dewdew kwan-da

translations.text: and take their clothes," the newcomers said.

forms.text: asa panisiringen-da kari ka-ma-kungu mu-ka-di-mi-lis-an kwan-da nu tau

translations.text: One of them was the leader. The newcomer said, "Get out! Why don't you move?"
The foreigner replied, "It doesn't make any difference whether I move or not. I won't move!"

forms.text: u nak-nakem nu tau i-kongu na-di-mi-lis-i

translations.text: Then they wondered, "Why doesn't he move?"

forms.text: ala amyan su uvay-da kwan-a nu ama-da

translations.text: "I know he has some gold," said their father.

forms.text: tuna-pi-lis-a kari kwan-a amyan su uvay-da lu lisnen-na amuri di-na-mi-lis-i

translations.text: Giving him a shove, he said, "Get out! There is some gold under his seat and that's why he doesn't move."

forms.text: ma-chita-na nu ama-da tunang-aep-a tu ni-lisnen-a k-aep-na-rana-sya nu ama-da

translations.text: When the father saw it, he grabbed it.

forms.text: u panisiringen-da-m tu-rana-lavi ikapaw-na uvay-da ni-aep nu tau

translations.text: The leader cried because he liked his gold that had been taken.

forms.text: malalayu-rana sira m-angay lu tatala emragbit

forms.text: amian su tau? nu-kakwa i-m-angay mengep su uvi?

translations.text: A long time ago, there was a person who went to get some potatoes.

forms.text: kuan-a nu anak-ne-m tu-lavi? si-ina si-ina kuan-a

translations.text: the child said to his father,

forms.text: yana-ni-aap nu kangkang lu kuang kuan-a

translations.text: The rooster took her far away."

forms.text: maniring s-ama-na-m uyuda nana-ni-aap nu kangkang

translations.text: The father said, "Oh, the rooster took her!"

forms.text: k-angay-da-rana lu tatala kalagen s-ina-na lu ilaud

translations.text: and they went to the boat to hunt for the mother in a foreign country.

forms.text: y-amian lu chia? su tau? kuan-ta

translations.text: "Is there anyone (of our own people) here?"

forms.text: kuan-ta nu tau? uri? lu ya-makarang a-takakal

translations.text: the child said, "Here you are, Mother!"
"You are not my child," said his mother.

forms.text: kuan-a nu anak-ne-m buken a si-ina-ku-imu kuan-a

translations.text: "Then you are not my mother?" said the child.

forms.text: maniring u anak-ne-m ni-salep-na-imu nu kangkang nu k-angay-ta mang-ali su uvi? siu? kuan-a

translations.text: "The rooster took you when we went to get some potatoes a long time ago."

forms.text: maniring s-ina-na-m ning kuan-a nuyud-ku-imu a anak-em mangwat-kamu su chinwat kuan-a

translations.text: His mother said, "If it's true you are my child, when boiling water is thrown on you
We'll see if you'll be killed."

forms.text: taktakana-rana u anak-na nu dinwat-em tongwus

translations.text: Boiling water was thrown on her child.

forms.text: maniring u ina-ne-m manuyung a anak-u-imu kuan-a

translations.text: "You're truly my child!" said his mother.

forms.text: mai-rana sira lu vagay-ta madiura u ina-na

translations.text: and returned to their house accompanied by the mother.

forms.text: maniring u ana-ne-m mengep ta-ka-mu su vatu kuan-a

translations.text: His father said, "Let's take some stones

forms.text: y-atei-ta su vagay-ta ta-manginanawa ta-ka-mu di-mai kuan-a

translations.text: and make the stone walls of our house, but be careful."

forms.text: ka-pangay-ta su aru dinalulut lu vagay-ta

translations.text: Then they put many spirit-weapons in their house

forms.text: mai-rana lu kangkang-em apuapuasena? u atei-na lu vagay-ta

translations.text: They went to the rooster's house and took stones from his house to their house (unctn).

forms.text: ingunguna u katawtaw-ne-m m-angay-rana lu ilaud u kangkang

translations.text: The rooster had gone to a foreign country.

forms.text: m-angay-ta lu takay mang-anak-u kwan-a ina-na

translations.text: "Let us both go to the field, my child," said his mother.
She went to dig for gold.
She said to the child, "Come here." The mother goes.
The child sees the spirit take the mother up to the sky.

forms.text: lavi a nu anak-na s-ina-na k-auli-na

translations.text: "Where is your mother?" said his father.
"The spirit crept up and flew away with Mother."

forms.text: mang-ep su aru nu varit/yaked s-ama-na kavangepna?

translations.text: The father took many strips of bamboo,

forms.text: k-angay-na lu tatala katukad-na lu kwang

translations.text: went to the boat, and sailed far away.

forms.text: m-angay lu ilaud m-angay lu vagay nu kwaway

translations.text: They went to a foreign country to the spirit's house.

forms.text: lu kwang chitagen-a u aru nu tau

translations.text: Far away, they saw many people.
They saw his house in the foreign country.
"You go home to your own people,"

forms.text: kwan-a karwan nu tau lu ilaud
ku-mi-chitagen nu mavakes-ku naket-na nu kwaway

translations.text: "I see the spirit captured my wife."

forms.text: m-angay-ka lu makarang nu tukun kwan-a nu tau

translations.text: "You go to the stilt house on the mountain," the foreigner said,
"and see there how your wife is being cared for."
"Who are you coming here to look for your mother?

forms.text: nak-nakem-ku-inyu? anak nu yamen lu yami

translations.text: I think that you are a child of us Yami people.
I wonder if you are really our child, dear.

forms.text: su pasavuren-ku dinwen nu maumlesan su chinwat-an

translations.text: then you are not our child."
She washed him and the child was fine, so she said, "You are really our child."
"Let's go and see them catching fish."
She made a hat, and went

forms.text: nu vagay-na nu apia nu k-anak-an

translations.text: "You are going, dear child," said his mother.

forms.text: m-angay-ka chyaa? nu apia tau kwan

translations.text: It doesn't matter if you do go. They are good people over there.

forms.text: apia nun m-angay-ku-rana kwan m-angay kalilyan u vaunda

translations.text: "Yes, good people; so I'll go," he said, and went to the plain (where the mother had been taken up).
The child cries, "You are so very tall. (unctn)
I'm afraid, because I'm just little."(unctn)
"I don't want to; I am not going, because Mother will scold us.

forms.text: y-abu m-angay-ku mwama tu kungyan avay-aken ina

translations.text: I'm not going to do planting in the mountains. Mother will scold me.
I'm going to look for something here in the trees."
"Then I'll cut off your mother's head. That's why I'm going."
"I don't want you to. I musn't let mother's head be cut off.
I'm going to cut off your mother's head."
"Yes," and the child began to cry.
After five days, he cut off her head.
and cried, "Your mother's blood is flowing down.
They went home and combed their hair
He saw the mother's spirit, and she said, "You were not bad.
My head was cut off and are you crying?
Look at me." "Let us both go,"
"Excuse me, Machinara, I'm going to sit by our betel nut basket.
